SECTION CHECK   Test yourself
SC310-1  What is the purpose of pro forma financial statements?
A.	To report last year's results to shareholders
B.	To replace the cash budget
C.	To calculate the tax due
D.	To show what the financial statements would look like if the plan happens
SC310-2  The pro forma statement of cash flows ends at a different cash figure from the cash budget. What does this mean?
A.	Both are correct; they measure different things
B.	There is an error in one of them
C.	The cash budget should be ignored
D.	Depreciation was added back
Answers and explanations are at the end of the chapter.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: three more assumptions
If volume falls 5%, operating income falls to $2,811,000. If concentrate costs 10% more, the margin falls from $8.20 to $7.66 a case and income to $2,694,000. Figure F310-04 shows each case, and Figure F310-05 compares them.

YOUR TURN   Both at once
Complete the last column of Figure F310-06, where volume falls and concentrate costs more. Answers are at the end of the chapter.

EXAM TRAP   Fixed costs stay fixed
In a scenario, fixed costs do not change with volume and the variable cost per unit does not change unless the question says so. Changing both at once is the commonest error in sensitivity questions.

EXAM TRAP   Depreciation and asset purchases
Depreciation is added back in the operating section because it reduced profit without using cash. The purchase of the filling line is an investing outflow, not an operating one.
